newsitem.title: UK: HSBC TARGET SARACEN SAYS RECEIVED APPROACHES.
newsitem.headline: HSBC TARGET SARACEN SAYS RECEIVED APPROACHES.

text.p: Saracen Value Trust, the subject of a management takeover bid from HSBC Investment Management, said on Tuesday it has been approached by other firms and it wants time to asses other alternatives.
"We are not convinced that HSBC is the best solution for our shareholders. There are better solutions for Saracen shareholders and we need time to assess," SFM fund manager Jim Fisher told Reuters.
These alternative solutions could include a restructuring of the trust, returning cash to shareholders, or employing other managers, he said.

Saracen said in a statement that it would writing to shareholders about a meeting held with HSBC on Monday and about approaches from "a number of other...fund managers as well as substantial investment management groups."
HSBC Asset Management said last Thursday it wanted to replace SFM Investment Management as the fund manager of the 81 million stg Saracen Value Trust.
Saracen said it has met with HSBC and been notified that shareholders representing 37.5 percent of shares are supporting HSBC's proposals to remove the board of Saracen and replace SFM with HSBC.
Saracen shares were trading at 95 pence, up from 89 at last Wednesday's close but a discount to the trust's net asset value (NAV) of 109.82 pence per share.
This is the latest in a recent string of investment trusts to come under pressure to make changes to enhance shareholder value.
Last week, investors bid shares of Govett Oriental Investment Trust up to a 52-week high on news that U.S. arbitrageur Sierra Trading had taken a 10 percent holding.
HSBC Asset Management said in a statement it was proposing to waive its management fee for the first two years of any contract.
After that, HSBC also will reduce the management fee to 75 bps from the current 100 bps of total assets less liabilities.
